title: Scalable Multiscale Manifold Alignment (QR-Free)

context.summary: Current multiscale manifold alignment based on diffusion wavelets is blocked by repeated modified QR on dyadic operator powers. We need a production implementation that scales from small graphs to very large sparse graphs while preserving existing package interfaces.
paper_alignment: Use Wang and Mahadevan joint Laplacian construction over multiple domains.
Retain the operator construction intent from T = F^+ Z L Z^T (F^T)^+.
Replace QR-heavy diffusion wavelet compression with practical scalable alternatives grounded in symmetric PSD assumptions.
codebase_constraints: Keep public entry points S3-style and compatible with existing method families (hyperdesign/list/default).
Follow control-object pattern: foo_control() plus resolve_foo_control().
Return class must remain multiblock_biprojector with method-specific subclass and extras.
Reuse matrix-free and operator-first style already present in kema_scalable and lowrank_align operator backend.

problem_statement.current_state: QR-based diffusion wavelet hierarchy is computationally prohibitive for large dimensions and large node counts.
problem_statement.target_state: A QR-free or QR-light multiscale hierarchy that is numerically stable, matrix-free, and compatible with current manifoldalign interfaces.
why_now: Need one implementation path that works from ~400 nodes to ~1M nodes.
Need to preserve scientific intent of multiscale manifold alignment while removing the main bottleneck.

goals: Implement scalable multiscale basis construction for symmetric PSD joint operators.
Support two interchangeable backends: spectral hierarchy (Theorem-3-equivalent) and randomized DWT-style hierarchy.
Integrate into the existing KEMA pipeline without breaking current API behavior.
Provide deterministic, testable outputs and diagnostics across scales.
non_goals: No rewrite of unrelated alignment methods.
No mandatory GPU dependency in first release.
No requirement to fully materialize dense N x N operators.
No guarantee that million-node benchmarks run in CI by default.

users_and_use_cases.need: Run multiscale alignment on medium datasets with strict reproducibility.
users_and_use_cases.success_metric: Stable embeddings and mappings across runs with fixed seed.

users_and_use_cases.need: Run sparse graph alignment on very large node counts without QR blowups.
users_and_use_cases.success_metric: Pipeline completes with matrix-free operations and bounded memory.

in_scope: Multiset joint graph/Laplacian assembly for S domains.
Low-rank per-domain compression of X^(s) D_s^(1/2).
Matrix-free operator T apply via compressed factors.
Backend A: spectral hierarchy from iterative eigensolvers.
Level-wise mapping extraction and result packaging.

proposed_api.integration_mode: Implement as a dedicated method family; do not overload kema semantics.
compatibility_requirements: New method follows package S3 conventions and result contracts.

pipeline: Build within-domain sparse symmetric kNN graphs and Laplacians.
Build multiset joint Laplacian L from within-domain and correspondence edges.
Compute per-domain truncated SVD of X^(s) D_s^(1/2).
Assemble implicit compressed operator T via V^T D^(-1/2) L D^(-1/2) V.
Run selected multiscale backend to produce nested bases Phi_j.
Derive level-wise mappings and embeddings; package result.

backend_a_spectral.description: Use iterative eigensolver on T and create levels by thresholding spectral decay over dyadic times.
pros: Most direct with symmetric PSD assumptions.
cons: Requires stable eigensolver tuning for large condition numbers.

backend_b_randomized_dwt.description: Approximate diffusion-wavelet compression with randomized sketches and thin QR on sketches only.

numerical_stability: Use symmetric operator checks and explicit regularization floors.
Avoid explicit pseudo-inverse materialization; use shift-invert or equivalent regularized operators.
Expose tolerances and fallback behavior in control.
performance_strategy: Block matvec interfaces; avoid explicit Z materialization.
Float32 optional path for large-scale performance.
Operator-based computations preferred over dense matrix assembly.

implementation_plan.name: Compressed operator core
deliverables: unit tests for operator correctness vs explicit small cases

implementation_plan.name: Backend B randomized DWT
deliverables: randomized range and sketched compression module

implementation_plan.name: Validation and docs
deliverables: testthat coverage for API, correctness, and backend parity on toy data

risks.risk: Eigensolver instability on poorly conditioned operators.
risks.mitigation: Regularization, solver fallback sequence, diagnostics in result object.
Oversampling defaults, residual checks, deterministic seeds, optional power iterations.

risks.risk: Memory pressure from dense feature operations.
risks.mitigation: Truncated ranks, block matvecs, optional feature compression pre-step.

risks.risk: Interface regressions in existing methods while adding a new multiscale entry point.
risks.mitigation: Dedicated method namespace and compatibility tests for existing methods.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Existing methods remain behaviorally unchanged after adding multiscale_manifold_align().
acceptance_criteria.verification: Regression smoke tests for existing methods and class contracts.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: multiscale_manifold_align_control() validates inputs and resolve_multiscale_manifold_align_control() rejects unknown fields.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Unit tests for valid construction, invalid values, and unknown-key failures.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: For small synthetic multiset cases, matrix-free apply_T matches explicit operator multiplication within relative error <= 1e-6.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Numerical equivalence unit tests on randomly generated small problems.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Backend A returns nested level bases with strictly non-increasing dimensions p_j.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Unit test checking p_(j+1) <= p_j across all levels.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Backend B returns nested level bases and uses only thin QR on sketch matrices (no full QR on operator dimension).
acceptance_criteria.verification: Code-path test and dimensional assertions in randomized hierarchy module tests.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: On toy datasets, Backend A and Backend B produce aligned subspaces with principal-angle similarity >= 0.9 on the top-k shared components.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Subspace overlap test using SVD of cross-basis products.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Output remains multiblock_biprojector-compatible and includes multiscale metadata fields when enabled.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Class tests and field presence checks.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: With fixed seed and same control settings, repeated runs produce equivalent level dimensions and numerically close bases (up to sign/rotation).
No non-finite values in level bases, mappings, or returned scores under standard test configurations.
On benchmark-gated medium synthetic data (>= 10k nodes total), spectral backend completes without dense N x N materialization.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Benchmark-gated smoke test with memory-safe instrumentation.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Operator modules expose block-matvec interfaces and sparse graph storage compatible with >= 1e6-node workflows.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Static checks of data structures and benchmark-gated construction test.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: User-facing docs include backend selection guidance, key controls, and examples for hyperdesign/list inputs.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Doc tests and manual review checklist pass.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: If a selected backend fails due to solver issues, error messages are actionable and include recommended control adjustments.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Negative tests that trigger controlled failures and inspect error text.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: kema_aligner -> fit_many.kema_aligner path can invoke multiscale mode via forwarded arguments.
Level-wise mappings are available for downstream embedding or transform application and have expected dimensions per domain.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Dimension and application tests on synthetic multiset examples.

definition_of_done: All mandatory acceptance criteria AC-001 through AC-009 pass in standard test runs.
Benchmark-gated checks AC-010 and AC-011 pass when benchmark mode is enabled.
Documentation and examples are published with the new controls.
No regression in existing kema and adapter tests.
open_questions: Default backend for first release: spectral only or spectral plus randomized as experimental?
How aggressive should default per-domain rank truncation be for heterogeneous feature dimensions?
Do we expose feature-level mapping reconstruction in v1 or node-space embeddings only?
